About this template

A daily vehicle inspection form is a document used by service workers to inspect vehicles on a daily basis. Whether you’re a police officer, a building inspector, or a worker for a large fleet, use this free Daily Vehicle Inspection Form to make sure your vehicles are up to code — and your team is working safely! Just customize the questions and add your logo and colors to make it your own.

With Jotform’s free Mobile Forms app, you can collect vehicle inspection reports from any device. You can even customize your form to send feedback to your other accounts! If you’d like to automate data collection further, get more out of your forms with our free Form Builder — add the information you need, get PDFs emailed to you, and sync submissions to your favorite apps. You can use Jotform Tables or Jotform Report Builder to analyze your inspections and see your work differently. Keep your team and vehicles safe and on task with a free Daily Vehicle Inspection Form.

About Vehicle Inspection Forms

Vehicle Inspection Forms are specialized documents designed to systematically record the condition, safety, and compliance status of vehicles. These forms are commonly used by automotive professionals, fleet managers, rental agencies, dealerships, and even individual vehicle owners to ensure that vehicles meet regulatory standards and are safe for operation. Typical use cases include pre-purchase inspections, routine maintenance checks, end-of-lease assessments, accident damage reports, and daily fleet safety inspections. By providing a structured checklist, these forms help users identify potential issues, document findings, and maintain a record for future reference or compliance purposes.

With Jotform, users can easily create, customize, and manage Vehicle Inspection Forms online without any coding knowledge. Leveraging Jotform’s intuitive drag-and-drop Form Builder, users can add fields for vehicle details, inspection checklists, photos, signatures, and more. The platform’s extensive template library and integration options streamline the data collection process, making it simple to store, organize, and share inspection results. Whether you’re managing a large fleet or conducting occasional inspections, Jotform’s features ensure efficient, accurate, and accessible vehicle inspection workflows.

Use Cases of Vehicle Inspection Forms

Vehicle Inspection Forms serve a wide range of industries and scenarios, each with unique requirements and challenges. Here’s how these forms can be tailored to different use cases, who typically uses them, and how their content may vary:

1. Possible Use Cases:
Pre-purchase Inspections: Used by buyers or dealerships to assess a vehicle’s condition before sale.
Routine Maintenance Checks: Employed by fleet managers or service centers to ensure ongoing vehicle safety and performance.
Rental Vehicle Inspections: Utilized by rental agencies to document vehicle condition before and after rental periods.
Accident or Damage Reports: Used by insurance agents or drivers to record details after an incident.
Regulatory Compliance Checks: Required by transportation companies to meet legal safety standards.
2. Problem Solving Points:
Ensure thorough and consistent inspections.
Reduce liability by maintaining accurate records.
Streamline communication between inspectors, managers, and clients.
Facilitate compliance with industry regulations.
3. Possible Owners and Users:
Automotive technicians and mechanics
Fleet and logistics managers
Car rental and leasing companies
Insurance adjusters
Individual vehicle owners
4. Differences of Creation Methods:
Pre-purchase forms may focus on detailed mechanical and cosmetic checks.
Routine maintenance forms often include recurring service items and mileage tracking.
Rental inspection forms typically have before-and-after checklists and photo upload fields.
Accident report forms require fields for incident details, witness statements, and damage photos.
Compliance forms may include regulatory checklists and digital signatures.

In summary, Vehicle Inspection Forms can be adapted to fit a variety of needs, ensuring that every inspection is thorough, standardized, and well-documented.

How to Create a Vehicle Inspection Form

Creating a Vehicle Inspection Form with Jotform is a straightforward process that can be tailored to your specific use case, whether you’re managing a fleet, running a rental agency, or conducting individual vehicle checks. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you design an effective and efficient inspection form:

1. Start with the Right Template or a Blank Form:
Visit your Jotform dashboard and click “Create.”
Choose “Form” and either start from scratch or select a relevant template from Jotform’s extensive library of Vehicle Inspection Forms.
Templates can save time and ensure you include all necessary fields for your specific scenario.
2. Select the Appropriate Layout:
Decide between a Classic Form (all questions on one page) for comprehensive inspections or a Card Form (one question per page) for guided, step-by-step checks.
3. Add Essential Form Elements:
Use the drag-and-drop builder to include fields such as:
Vehicle identification (make, model, year, VIN)
Odometer reading
Inspection date and inspector’s name
Checklist items (tires, brakes, lights, fluids, etc.)
Condition ratings (pass/fail, good/fair/poor)
File upload for photos of the vehicle or specific issues
Signature fields for inspector and/or vehicle owner
4. Customize for Your Use Case:
For pre-purchase inspections, add detailed mechanical and cosmetic checklists.
For rental agencies, include before-and-after inspection sections and damage documentation.
For fleet management, add recurring maintenance items and service history tracking.
For accident reports, provide fields for incident description, location, and witness information.
5. Enhance Functionality with Widgets and Integrations:
Use widgets for e-signatures, image uploads, or barcode scanning.
Integrate with payment gateways if inspection fees are involved.
Connect to Jotform Tables or external tools for data management and reporting.
6. Design and Branding:
Click the Paint Roller icon to access the Form Designer.
Adjust colors, fonts, and add your company logo to match your brand identity.
7. Set Up Notifications and Sharing:
Configure email notifications to alert relevant parties of new submissions.
Share your form via direct link, email, or embed it on your website for easy access.
8. Test and Launch:
Use the Preview feature to test your form’s functionality.
Submit a test entry to ensure all data is captured and notifications are working.

By following these steps, you can create a professional, user-friendly Vehicle Inspection Form that streamlines your inspection process, ensures compliance, and keeps your records organized and accessible.

Frequently Asked Questions
1. What is a Vehicle Inspection Form?

A Vehicle Inspection Form is a structured document used to assess and record the condition, safety, and compliance of a vehicle during inspections.

2. Why are Vehicle Inspection Forms important?

They help ensure vehicles are safe, meet regulatory standards, and provide a documented record for liability, maintenance, and compliance purposes.

3. What information is typically included in a Vehicle Inspection Form?

Common fields include vehicle details, inspection date, checklist items (e.g., brakes, lights, tires), condition ratings, photos, and signatures.

4. Are there different types of Vehicle Inspection Forms?

Yes, forms can be tailored for pre-purchase checks, routine maintenance, rental inspections, accident reports, and regulatory compliance.

5. Who uses Vehicle Inspection Forms?

Automotive professionals, fleet managers, rental agencies, insurance adjusters, and individual vehicle owners commonly use these forms.

6. How do Vehicle Inspection Forms help with compliance?

They provide a standardized way to document inspections, making it easier to meet industry regulations and pass audits.

7. Can Vehicle Inspection Forms be used for digital recordkeeping?

Absolutely. Digital forms allow for easy storage, retrieval, and sharing of inspection records, improving efficiency and reducing paperwork.

8. Are Vehicle Inspection Forms secure and private?

When using platforms like Jotform, data is securely stored and can be protected with access controls, ensuring privacy and compliance with data protection regulations.
